Bring enough firepower or a plan to open the truck quickly, and have a getaway vehicle and route ready before you start. One successful truck robbery with a clean escape unlocks the trophy. If the escape fails, the next armored truck you meet is another chance.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: armored trucks recur in the world, so a failed robbery or escape can be retried on the next one.

Check the map late in the game for any fogged or unvisited pocket and sweep those last. The trophy unlocks when the fifty-second area is explored.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official description calls this a partnership with mass appeal, so it belongs to the two protagonists acting together in a public-facing way. Watch for partnership moments as the story and free roam put the pair in front of an audience or a crowd-pleasing situation, and take part fully when one appears rather than skipping past it. Because the description is deliberately vague, treat any joint activity the game highlights for the pair as a candidate and finish it. trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This trophy is about choices made, for better or worse, and PlayStation tracks a count behind it that runs to 500. Choices are the decisions the game puts in front of you across the story and the world, so the practical route is to keep engaging with them rather than skipping optional decision points. Because each choice is made once in the moment it appears, a choice you never encounter cannot be gone back for in the same stretch of play. Keep choosing whenever the game asks and the count builds across the whole playthrough. The trophy unlocks when the tracked choices reach their target.
trophies.missableNote: Watch out: choices happen once, when the game presents them, and the tracked target is 500. Skipping optional content wholesale can leave you short of choices in a single playthrough, so engage with decision points as they appear instead of planning to mop them all up later.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: this trophy is built around succeeding on a second attempt after a first one went wrong. When something in the game gives you a retry after a failure, take the retry and succeed at it rather than reloading to erase the failure. The natural way to earn it is simply to keep playing after a failed attempt instead of save-scumming every mistake away. Once a second-try success registers, the trophy unlocks. If you play flawlessly for long stretches, a deliberate small failure followed by a clean retry creates the situation on purpose.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: failures and retries happen throughout the game, and the situation can be created deliberately by failing once and succeeding on the retry.

trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.guide: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, use a melee attack to knock a person down as you pass them, like a bowling pin. Speed is the usual reason this fails, so a gentle roll-past works better than a full-speed attempt. One clean knockdown with the melee drive-by unlocks the trophy.

Spending counts across every shop combined, so ordinary play moves this steadily: buy vehicles, gear, clothing and supplies as you actually need them rather than hoarding cash. If you reach the cleanup stage short of the target, deliberate shopping sprees close the gap quickly, and expensive purchases move the counter fastest. The total is cumulative and never goes down. The trophy unlocks when your lifetime shop spending reaches 100,000 dollars.
